cells.tense: You can hold several true things at once and still choose a direction.
cells.ask: Pick something you've been calling open, write it down as decided, and act on it today.
cells.core:
You're carrying more than one honest answer at a time, and none of them is crowding the others out. That's harder than it sounds — the usual failure is forcing an answer early or letting the pile grow until you can't move. You move. The direction you pick fits what you actually see, and it holds long enough to walk toward.

What bends is that you decide quietly and don't say which way you went. Then the people around you are working from a map they didn't get. Say the choice once, plainly, while you're still in the room — not the reasons behind it. The direction is already yours. Handing it over is what this balance is free to take on next.

cells.verb: Sorting many true things down to one direction
cells.place: At the point where direction gets chosen and held

cells.tense: You are trying to know the whole map before you pick a single road.
cells.ask: Name one direction you're following today, in a single sentence, without qualifying it.
cells.core:
You're reading everything at once. More angles, more versions, more voices that might be right — and the reading has become the work. Choosing doesn't survive that much looking. Each time you get close to picking, another true thing shows up and pulls the wheel back.

What you're guarding against is being wrong where it shows. That's a real risk, but the way you're avoiding it costs more than the mistake would. Enough is already in front of you to choose. What isn't present is the willingness to be steered by one light while the others stay visible. Pick the brightest one and let the rest wait.

cells.tense: You stood at a door that's now behind you and you're still deciding.
cells.ask: Tell one person the next place you're going before you know how you'll get there.
cells.core:
You can see a direction clearly and stay still beside it, treating that spot as the whole picture instead of a place you're standing. When this is working, you look at what you know, pick one path through it, and walk while the other answers stay true behind you. That's the shape you'd recognize. It's the shape you're not using.

You don't have to relitigate anything to move. You only have to say the next place out loud. Not a plan, not the whole route — just the next direction, said to someone who can hear it. That's how a still thing starts moving again. What you can see is still there. It's been waiting for you to use it.

cells.tense: You are already steering by what you know without saying you are.
cells.ask: Admit one choice you've already made and have been calling someone else's.
cells.core:
You're directing a lot of what happens around you. People take their cue from what you say and what you let pass, and you feel the weight of that. But ask who's steering and you'll say circumstances are, or the work is, or someone else's decision is. The steering is happening. Your name isn't on it.

This isn't about credit. It's that if you don't say you chose this, you can't un-choose it. The direction runs on without you, and you keep reacting to something you made. Saying it changes what you can do next. It puts the wheel back where it already is.
